jobs.occupation: Data Analyst with Focus on Magnetic Navigation – DTU Space
jobs.description:
Join DTU Space on magnetic navigation! 

Are you passionate about unravelling the mysteries of Earth’s magnetic field? Do you have a keen eye for detail, a self-motivated attitude, and strong problem-solving skills? If so, we invite you to apply for a researcher position at DTU Space, where you'll contribute to cutting-edge applications of Earth’s magnetic field.

The job
In this position, you'll work at the forefront of geomagnetic research, collaborating with an interdisciplinary team to developing advanced methods for using the geomagnetic field for navigation.

Our expectations of you
We’re seeking someone who: 

• 
has knowledge of Earth's magnetic field and its use in Navigation

• 
is experienced in using MATLAB for scientific programming and data processing

• 
has prior experience with solving Inverse Problems, Kalman Filtering, and algorithms used for Navigation using Earth’s magnetic field

In addition to technical expertise, we value a team player who communicates effectively, thrives in a collaborative environment, and takes initiative. 

What we offer in return
At DTU Space, you’ll be part of a dynamic and supportive research community dedicated to pushing the boundaries of science and technology. Your work will play an integral role in advancing our understanding of geomagnetism and its applications.

If you meet the qualifications above and are excited about contributing to this fascinating field, we’d love to hear from you.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Academic Officer, Senior Officer, Senior Executive Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The position is full-time in agreement with the candidate. The position is temporary, lasting until 31 December 2031. 

The starting date is 1 January 2027, or as mutually agreed.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 3 December 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact professor and head of the division of Geomagnetism and Geospace Nils Olsen, email nio@space.dtu.dk.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Space
The DTU Space Institute has about 250 employees and is located in the greater Copenhagen area at the Lyngby Campus of the Technical University of Denmark. We link natural science closely with the development of new technology. DTU Space is involved in the full life cycle of space activities, including concept and design, construction and prototyping, calibration and validation, implementation and operations, data analysis, processing, dissemination, and applications, leading to new instruments and applications. With the specialised and refined technology available, we are getting more and more answers and further insight about the Earth and the universe surrounding us. We contribute to about 200 scientific publications a year.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

What if your commercial expertise could help shape the future of offshore wind and wildlife protection?

At DHI, we combine science, technology and engineering to address some of the world's most pressing environmental challenges.

We are looking for commercially minded Contract Managers to support the growth of MUSE's international project portfolio. In this role, you will work closely with project leaders and senior stakeholders to manage complex contractual arrangements, safeguard commercial interests and strengthen contractual governance across projects – all in support of successful project delivery.

This is an opportunity to apply your commercial and contractual expertise in a growing business at the intersection of offshore renewable energy, engineering and advanced technology, while helping build the foundations for scalable project delivery.

About DHI MUSE

DHI MUSE develops and delivers some of the world's most advanced bird and wildlife monitoring systems for offshore wind farms. Our solutions support developers, operators and regulators in understanding and mitigating environmental impacts while enabling the growth of renewable energy.

As a dedicated business unit within DHI's global organisation, MUSE brings together experts in offshore wind, engineering, software development, data analytics and ecology to deliver innovative monitoring solutions across international markets.

Responsibilities and Challenges

As Contract Manager, you will act as a trusted contractual and commercial advisor to Project Managers, the Project Portfolio Director and senior leadership within MUSE. You will support complex project-based engagements involving offshore wind developers, engineering teams, hardware and software suppliers, installation contractors and other project stakeholders.

You will provide contractual and commercial guidance throughout the project lifecycle, from tender and pre-award through execution, installation, commissioning, operational handover, operations and maintenance and project close-out. Applying sound professional judgement and commercial awareness, you will help protect project profitability, manage contractual risks and opportunities, and strengthen commercial outcomes across the portfolio.

The main responsibilities are to:

• Act as contractual and commercial advisor to Project Managers, the Project Portfolio Director and senior leadership across MUSE.

• Lead contractual assessments and provide expert advice on contract structures, obligations, risk allocation, remedies and commercial terms throughout the project lifecycle.

• Support tendering and proposal processes and support or lead contractual negotiations with clients, partners, suppliers and subcontractors, , in close collaboration with Project Managers and Legal.

• Manage contractual change and commercial opportunity processes, including variation orders, extensions of time, amendments and claims.

• Identify contractual risks, commercial opportunities and potential impacts arising from project changes, technical interfaces and delivery requirements.

• Support contractual and commercial management of suppliers, subcontractors and project delivery partners, including installation, commissioning and operations and maintenance obligations.

• Work closely with Project Managers to manage contractual obligations, delivery interfaces and commercial outcomes across complex technical projects.

• Ensure compliance with DHI policies, governance requirements and Levels of Authority.

• Collaborate with Legal, Finance, Technology & Innovation and project stakeholders on contractual matters and commercial decision-making.

• Contribute to the continuous improvement and development of MUSE contract standards, playbooks, templates and commercial project practices.

What We're Looking For

Required education, experience and capabilities

• 5–8+ years of relevant experience in contract management, commercial management or a similar project-based role, preferably within offshore wind or a comparable business area.

• Experience supporting complex technical projects, preferably within an international and multi-jurisdictional environment.

• A Master's or Bachelor's degree in Law, Business Administration, Engineering, Commercial Management or a related discipline.

• Strong understanding of contractual risk and opportunity management, claims, variations, amendments and commercial project drivers.

• Demonstrated ability to interpret contractual terms, assess commercial and operational implications and develop practical recommendations.

• Experience preparing contractual correspondence, managing notice requirements and maintaining clear records to support variations, claims and contractual compliance.

• Experience advising Project Managers and senior stakeholders on contractual matters and supporting decisions within delegated authority.

• Strong negotiation skills and confidence in client-facing contractual and commercial discussions.

• Experience working with project delivery teams, suppliers, subcontractors and other external stakeholders. Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal.

• Sound professional judgement, with the ability to work independently, balance competing project priorities and communicate contractual issues clearly to non-legal stakeholders.

Additional experience and strengths, contributing to success in this role

• Experience within offshore wind, offshore energy, engineering, IT and technology, infrastructure, environmental consulting or other complex project-driven industries.

• Experience with EPC, EPIC or EPCI delivery models, or other complex engineering and technology project contracts.

• Exposure to hardware and software integrated systems, installation, commissioning or operational delivery projects.

• Familiarity with contractual requirements associated with system integration, testing, commissioning, installation, maintenance and customer acceptance.

• A background in mechanical engineering or a strong understanding of technology development and delivery, including software, networking, hardware or engineering systems.

• Experience identifying gaps between client commitments and supplier or subcontractor obligations, and aligning relevant requirements across the contractual chain.

• Familiarity with international contractual frameworks and commercial governance.

• Experience developing or improving contract standards, templates or commercial management processes.

• Additional language capabilities supporting international client and stakeholder collaboration.

Why join DHI?

To work at DHI means being part of an organisation that is the global leader in solving the world's toughest challenges in water, environment and sustainability.

In this position, we offer you the opportunity to join a growing business unit with dedicated colleagues to:

• Support some of the most advanced wildlife monitoring projects in the offshore wind industry.

• Take on a visible commercial role influencing contractual outcomes and project profitability across an international portfolio.

• Collaborate with leading experts in offshore wind, engineering, software development, hardware systems and ecology.

• A highly international working environment with colleagues and clients across Europe and beyond.

• Professional and personal development opportunities within a global knowledge organisation.

• Flexible working arrangements.

• Help shape MUSE's commercial governance and contract management practices as the business continues to grow.

DHI is a global and independent company dedicated to working on challenges within the fields of water, environment and sustainability. Within these fields, we provide a wide range of advisory, digital advisory, research and water governance services as well as providing leading-edge MIKE technologies and products to the market. At DHI, we are constantly looking for passionate and talented people who are eager to join our team.

By joining DHI, you will not only become part of a dynamic and collaborative global team of experts; you will be empowered to innovate, engage and grow in your area of expertise. DHI is committed to disseminating our knowledge effectively and across our worldwide network of offices.

Location & Mobility

• The role is based at DHI offices in Denmark, with flexible working opportunities in accordance with DHI policy.

• Travelling must be expected in the role to enable collaboration with clients and/or inside DHI.

How to apply

• Please submit your application including CV via the relevant job posting on DHI's website: http://www.dhigroup.com/careers

• Application deadline: 18th December 2026

• For further information, please contact Yong Quan Lim, Talent Acquisition by email: liyq@dhigroup.com / Carsten Baun Hoest, PMO & Project Portfolio Director, MUSE by email: caun@dhigroup.com.

**

Data centres are a strategic growth area at COWI. As we scale our presence in this market, we are enhancing our multidisciplinary capabilities and working closely with clients to develop reliable, efficient and sustainable data centre solutions. • Engage in dialogue with customers to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions.

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

On top of that, you will have:

• A relevant educational background in engineering.

• Experience working with design of data centres, engineering consultancy, technical advisory or complex infrastructure projects.

• Experience from data centre projects or other large-scale mission critical projects.

• Professional proficiency in English.

Additional role-specific qualifications may include:

• Experience with mechanical systems for data centres.

• Experience working with large-scale infrastructure or industrial facilities.

• Experience leading technical teams or complex engineering projects.

**Work location.

**

The role can be based in any of our offices across Scandinavia. This includes offices in:

Norway – Bergen, Trondheim, Stavanger, Oslo and Fredrikstad

Sweden – Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmö

Denmark – Copenhagen, Kongens Lyngby, Vejle, Aarhus, Odense and Aalborg

We work in international and multidisciplinary teams, and many of our projects are delivered across offices and borders.

**Do you have more questions?

**

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Mette Gutte at mtgt@cowi.com. Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com and www.arkitema.com where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

**A place to work and so much more

**

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers. We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home. With offices primarily located in Scandinavia, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

**Before you apply

**

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture. We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis, so the role may close as soon as we find the right match.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key

**

We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

jobs.occupation: 172948 Associate Professor of Structural Molecular Biology
jobs.description:
Department of Biotech Research and Innovation Center
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
 University of Copenhagen

  The University seeks to appoint an associate professor to the Department of Biotech Research and Innovation Center to commence on 1 April 2027.

  Information on the Department can be found at: https://sund.ku.dk/.

  Job description

  The associate professor has a strong track record in cryo-electron microscopy analysis of mitochondrial and herpesviral nucleic acid-protein complexes, including fundamental insights into mitochondrial protein synthesis and herpesvirus DNA replication. The candidate will further develop his/her research into a leading programme on mitochondrial and viral genome maintenance and gene expression to advance our mechanistic understanding of mitochondrial DNA replication, RNA quality control and DNA replication mechanisms across human herpesviruses. In his/her line of research, the candidate will combine biochemistry, biophysics, and single-particle cryo-EM to explore the mechanisms of action of the involved macromolecular complexes. Moreover, the candidate has demonstrated the ability to organize and teach practical cryo-EM-related courses. 

  The associate professor is expected to play an active role in strengthening BRIC's research and training environment, including supervision and mentoring of early-career researchers and engagement in BRIC's postdoctoral career development activities. The successful candidate will also contribute to academic leadership, committee work and other organizational activities within the department and faculty.

  The associate professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination 	
• Research-based teaching, including associated examination 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of researchers 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments   Required qualifications 
 To be qualified for an associate professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• Research qualifications at the level that can be achieved by satisfactorily completing a period of employment as an assistant professor/postdoc, but may also be obtained in other ways 	
• Teaching qualifications and pedagogical competencies 	
• Research-based teaching   The associate professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Terms of employment
 The position is permanent.

  The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). 

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Questions
 For further information, please contact Director Anders H. Lund, BRIC-director@bric.ku.dk

  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

  Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application (Including motivations for applying for the position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD, and other relevant certificates) 	
• A complete list of publications  	
• Research plan (3‐5 pages) 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines)   Application procedure
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, 16 December 2026.

**WHY SPEKTR

**At spektr, we are on a mission to automate the world’s most complex compliance workflows through AI. Founded by the team behind HelloFlow (acquired by Trulioo), spektr is building the infrastructure and AI agents to run compliance at scale.

_Compliance, built like product.

_Financial services has changed enormously. Much of the technology behind compliance hasn’t. Teams still spend hours on manual checks, disconnected systems slow down launches, and entering a new market can mean rebuilding the same processes all over again.

We’re changing that. spektr gives regulated businesses one platform for onboarding, monitoring and investigations, with configurable workflows and AI agents that do the legwork. Product, Operations and Compliance can move together, with the control they need to grow.

It’s a huge opportunity in an industry that has moved slowly for too long. We’ve built a product we’re proud to put in front of the most demanding customers. Now we’re looking for people who want to help get it into their hands.

• $26M raised, including a $20M Series A led by NEA, with backing from Northzone, Seedcamp and PreSeed Ventures.

• Customers worth getting excited about. We work with businesses including Pleo, Trustly, Nexi and Santander. These are large accounts with complex problems, ambitious teams and plenty of room for us to make a difference.

• Three offices: Copenhagen, London and Iași, with customers across more than 15 countries.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**We are looking for an AI Engineer who is, first and foremost, a product builder. In this role, you won't just be running experiments in a notebook; you will own the end-to-end AI strategy and its direct impact on our customers.

In this role, you will own everything related to AI, LLMs, and intelligent automation.

This is a high-impact role in a fast-growing company. We are looking for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, loves solving complex compliance puzzles, and is eager to shape the next generation of compliance technology.

**What You Will Be Doing

**

• AI Strategy & Ownership: Own the end-to-end AI roadmap—from selecting the right models (SOTA commercial vs. fine-tuned open source) to deciding how they are integrated into the product core.

• Agentic Feature Design: Design and deploy LLM-powered features including autonomous agents, advanced RAG pipelines, and intelligent document understanding.

• Product-Led AI: Collaborate directly with founders to translate complex compliance "puzzles" into scalable AI solutions. You own the "Why" behind every model choice.

• Continuous Innovation: Stay at the bleeding edge of AI/ML research, proactively identifying new papers or releases that can give spektr a competitive advantage.

• Engineering for Reliability: Turn non-deterministic AI outputs into deterministic product value. You ensure our agents are accurate, explainable, and hallucination-free.

**What We Are Looking For

**

• The Product Mindset: You are a product person at heart. You care about whether the AI actually solves the user's problem, not just if the loss curve is going down.

• High-Agency Builder: You prefer building systems over following manuals. You identify bottlenecks in our AI workflows and fix them before they become tickets.

• AI/ML Expertise: 2+ years of experience in ML, AI, or Data/Backend roles with a deep understanding of modern LLM stacks.

• Technical Mastery: Strong skills in TypeScript (our core) and/or Python, with hands-on experience in frameworks like LangChain or equivalent orchestration layers.

• RAG & Vector Mastery: You’ve built production-grade RAG pipelines and understand the nuances of embedding, retrieval strategy, and re-ranking.

• Evaluation Obsession: You understand that "it works on my machine" doesn't apply to LLMs. You have experience setting up evaluation frameworks to measure and improve model performance.

• Cloud & Scale: Experience deploying AI services in AWS or containerized environments, ensuring they are scalable and cost-effective.

• Communication: You can explain the trade-offs of a specific model architecture to a founder and a technical bottleneck to a peer with equal clarity.

**OUR TECH INTERESTS

**

• Models: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Open Source (LLaMA, Mistral).

• Stack: TypeScript, Python, LangChain, etc

• Infra: AWS, Kubernetes, CI/CD for LLMs.

**OUR PROCESS

**

• Intro call with our Talent team (30 minutes)

• Technical Interview (30 minutes)

• Technical Interview (60 minutes)

**How To Apply

**We hire the smartest, kindest, and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work. You’ll be joining a team with a proven track record and the "Product-Market Fit" to change an entire industry.

spektr is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, disability, sexual orientation or any other characteristic, and we assess every candidate against the same role requirements.

We are currently looking for an ambitious Account Manager in Copenhagen who is motivated by delivering results, building strong client relationships and developing their career within a company with high ambitions.

jobs.occupation: Head of Group Compliance & Group Data Protection Officer
jobs.description:
**Lead a global compliance function and help shape how compliance enables the business

**Are you an experienced compliance, privacy or GRC leader who enjoys operating at the intersection of regulation, business and technology?

Do you thrive in a role where you can set direction, lead experienced professionals, advise Executive Management and the Board, and turn complex requirements into practical solutions?

Then this could be your opportunity to lead Aeven's Group Compliance function.

**The role

**As Head of Group Compliance & Group Data Protection Officer, you will lead the Global Group Compliance organisation of approximately 27 professionals across four teams and three countries.

You will have overall responsibility for the strategy, direction and development of the function, covering:

• Group Data Protection and the DPO function

• Regulatory Compliance

• Enterprise Risk Management

• Internal Audit

• ISO and external assurance

• Customer and supplier assurance

• Responsibility / ESG

You will lead primarily through your managers, creating clear priorities and accountability while empowering highly specialised teams to own their areas.

The role combines strategic leadership, independent oversight and senior business advisory. You will work closely with Executive Management and the Board, providing a consolidated view of Aeven's compliance, privacy, risk and assurance position and highlighting where action or decisions are required.

At the same time, you will work closely with the business to translate regulatory and customer requirements into clear, proportionate and commercially workable solutions.

****Your responsibilities

• Set the strategy, priorities and roadmap for Group Compliance and lead, coach and develop the management team.

• Advise Executive Management and the Board on significant compliance, privacy and risk matters and provide clear, decision-oriented Management Information.

• Act as Group DPO and oversee Aeven's data protection framework, including significant privacy risks, breaches, regulatory engagement and international transfers.

• Lead the organisation's approach to regulatory developments, including GDPR, NIS2, DORA-related customer requirements, AI Act, Data Act and digital sovereignty.

• Own the Enterprise Risk Management framework and consolidated enterprise risk view, while ensuring risk ownership remains with the business.

• Oversee Internal Audit and Aeven's broader certification and assurance landscape, including ISO and ISAE activities.

• Provide senior oversight of customer and supplier due diligence, audits and regulatory assurance requirements.

• Support significant incidents, investigations, escalations and remediation across the organisation.

• Continuously develop and modernise the function through simplification, automation, better Management Information and effective use of compliance technology.

A key part of the role is ensuring that compliance enables the business rather than unnecessarily slowing it down.

****Your experience

****We are looking for an experienced leader who is comfortable operating where regulation, risk and business strategy meet.

You bring:

• A relevant Master's degree, for example in Law, Business/Commercial Law or a related field.

• 10+ years of experience within compliance, data protection, GRC or a related area, including several years leading managers and international or multi-disciplinary teams.

• Strong GDPR and data protection expertise, including DPO experience.

• Proven experience advising C-level executives and Boards and communicating complex risks through clear Management Information.

• Experience with Enterprise Risk Management, Internal Audit and assurance.

• Working knowledge of ISO management systems (ISO9001, ISO27001 and ISO14001) and ideally ISAE 3000/3402 reporting.

• Knowledge of EU digital and cyber regulation, including NIS2, DORA, AI Act and Data Act.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

Experience from an international, regulated or technology-driven organisation is an advantage, as is experience with privacy certification, GRC technology, customer assurance, ESG or transformation.

**Who You Are

**You are a trusted and credible advisor who can challenge senior stakeholders constructively while building strong relationships across the organisation.

You lead through trust, clear direction and empowerment, and enjoy developing managers and creating high-performing teams.

You are strategic but pragmatic, with strong business understanding and the judgement to balance regulatory robustness with commercial realities.

You communicate complex issues simply, drive follow-through and are comfortable raising risks and challenging established ways of working.

Most importantly, you bring integrity, sound judgement, independence and a genuine desire to make compliance work for the business.

**Why Aeven?

**This is an opportunity to take on a broad and influential leadership role at the centre of Aeven's governance and business operations.

You will lead a highly skilled international team, work directly with senior leadership and the Board, and help shape how a technology-driven organisation responds to an increasingly complex regulatory environment.

If you are motivated by leadership, influence, complexity and the opportunity to make compliance a genuine business enabler, we would like to hear from you.

This is a role for someone who can hold a genuinely complex domain in their head and then explain it in three sentences to a customer who has never heard the phrase “patent exhaustion.”

Experience level: a deep specialist role. We expect solid, hands-on experience with cellular device approvals and licensing — likely 10+ years across regulatory, certification, or IP/licensing work in mobile, IoT, or telecom hardware. This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports, high autonomy, and direct executive visibility.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

****What's in it for you?

• A domain you will own, not administer. IoT Cellular License, SEP and certification strategy is an executive-level topic at Trackunit right now, with real financial exposure attached. You will not be filing paperwork in a corner, you will be shaping the position the company takes.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

****What you'll do

****Your work splits roughly into four parts: licensing, approvals, guidance, and governance.

• Own our SEP position. Understand where our cellular SEP exposure actually sits across our device portfolio, track the relevant patent pools and licensing programmes, and maintain a clear, evidence-based view of what is covered through our supply chain and what is not.

• Run supplier licensing due diligence. Establish and maintain a consistent set of asks across module suppliers — coverage confirmation, standards and generations covered, and honest disclosure of known gaps — so responses can be compared side by side and fed into supplier qualification.

• Support licensing negotiations and claims. Work alongside our General Counsel, external patent counsel, and economic advisors on royalty basis questions, valuation and apportionment arguments, and claims that reach us through our OEM customers. You bring the technical and supply chain substance; they bring the legal strategy.

• Own global type approvals and certification. Plan and steer RED/CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, and the wider set of regional approvals, plus GCF/PTCRB and carrier certification, across a multi-region device portfolio. Keep certification on the critical path of new product programmes rather than at the end of them.

• Stay ahead of regulatory change. Cyber Resilience Act, RED delegated acts, radio spectrum and network sunsets, environmental and product compliance requirements — know what is coming, when it bites, and what it means for our roadmap.

• Make the complex simple, and guide without over-promising. Write and maintain the internal playbooks, customer-facing explainers, and OEM guidance that turn this domain into something a commercial colleague or a customer can act on. Be the person Sales, Legal, and customers come to when a licensing notification lands, explaining the landscape accurately, saying clearly where the limits of our position are, and pointing customers to independent specialist advice where that is the right answer.

• Build the governance. Response protocols, decision records, escalation paths, and embedding licensing and compliance requirements into how we qualify suppliers and run the product development lifecycle.

****Who you are

****We think you'll need

• Strong working knowledge of cellular connectivity (e.g. LTE-M, NB-IoT, LTE Cat-1/1bis, 5G) and the direction of travel, plus a real understanding of the module and chipset landscape.

• Solid, practical experience with licensing and Standard Essential Patents in mobile or IoT devices: FRAND principles, patent pools, patent exhaustion and the limits of sublicensing, and how royalties are actually structured and argued.

• Hands-on experience with global type approvals and regulatory certification for radio products — RED/CE, FCC, and the regional approvals that come with selling hardware worldwide.

• Experience working across a hardware supply chain with module suppliers, test houses, notified bodies, and certification partners.

• Communication as a core skill, not a bonus. You can take a genuinely complicated subject and land it in plain language, in writing, with an audience that has no background in it.

• The judgement to know what we can and cannot say to a customer, and the discipline to hold that line even when it would be easier not to.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You are honest about uncertainty. In this domain, no one can offer a blanket guarantee, and the people who claim otherwise create problems later. We would rather be accurate than reassuring.

• You are curious and self-driven, this is a field that changes constantly, and nobody is going to hand you a reading list.

• You finish things. A clear one-page answer delivered this week beats a perfect analysis that arrives after the decision was made.

• You are comfortable being the only person in the room who knows a subject, and you use that position to make others smarter rather than to make yourself indispensable.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement, but a strong motivation and interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work, including MCP servers and agents against our own platform, and we see clear potential in applying it to research, documentation, and compliance workflows. We don't expect you to have experience with this but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

****How you'll grow here

****This is a specialist role with an unusually wide view of the business, and we've set it up that way on purpose.

• Executive proximity. You will work closely with the SVP of IoT Division, while reporting into a central function for IoT, as the Device Reliability Engineering. You will help in presenting to executive leadership on exposure, risk, and recommendations. Your analysis will inform on a product technical matter (Not Legal) but with real financial and commercial decisions.

• Cross-functional reach. Legal, Finance, Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Sales all depend on this domain. Few roles at Trackunit touch as many parts of the company.

• External network. You will work with external patent counsel, economic consultants, module suppliers, certification bodies, and industry forums — building a network that extends well beyond Trackunit.

• Room to define the function. This discipline is being built out now. What it becomes — and whether it grows into a team — is substantially yours to shape.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

jobs.description:
Are you an experienced software engineer looking for something different? Imagine developing software in the morning, testing it on real hardware in the afternoon, and eventually watching it take flight.

At Acodyne, you will work alongside engineers developing next-generation unmanned aircraft, applying your software engineering experience to challenges that extend far beyond the screen.

You will have the opportunity to work across the software stack, from embedded systems and flight control integration to simulation, telemetry, and ground-based applications. You'll join a small, ambitious team where your contributions will have a direct impact on the aircraft we build.

Your Role

As part of our growing engineering team, you will develop and integrate software for our high-speed, heavy-lift cargo UAVs and their supporting systems.

You will work closely with electronics, mechanical, and aerospace engineers to turn ideas into working solutions, taking software from development through simulation, hardware integration, and real-world flight testing.

We believe that reliable software starts with good engineering practices. Code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and reproducible builds are important parts of how we want to develop our systems.

You will:

• 
Develop and maintain software for our aircraft and supporting systems.

• 
Work with embedded Linux platforms, flight computers, sensors, actuators, and communication systems.

• 
Integrate and extend existing flight control technologies such as ArduPilot or PX4.

• 
Develop tools for telemetry collection, monitoring, data analysis, and ground control.

• 
Build and maintain simulation environments and automated tests to validate software before flight.

• 
Contribute to reliable development workflows, continuous integration, testing, and release processes.

• 
Collaborate across engineering disciplines to integrate and troubleshoot software and hardware.

• 
Participate in prototype development, system integration, and flight test activities.

• 
Document software designs, interfaces, and test results to support future certification and compliance.

About You

We're looking for an experienced software engineer who enjoys solving challenging technical problems and takes pride in building reliable, maintainable software.

You've worked in a professional software development environment and understand the value of good engineering practices. Version control, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and reproducible builds are a natural part of how you work.

You're comfortable taking ownership, making pragmatic engineering decisions, and collaborating with people from different technical backgrounds. You enjoy learning new technologies and aren't afraid to venture beyond your existing expertise.

You don't need to be an aerospace expert. We value strong software engineering fundamentals, technical curiosity, and the ability to master new domains.

You likely have:

• 
Several years of professional software development experience.

• 
Strong programming skills in C/C++ and experience developing software for Linux.

• 
Experience working with modern development workflows, including Git, code reviews, automated testing, and CI/CD.

• 
An understanding of software architecture, debugging, and maintaining complex software systems.

• 
Some experience with embedded systems, hardware interfaces, or resource-constrained environments.

• 
A pragmatic, hands-on approach to engineering and an interest in working with physical systems.

• 
The ability to work independently while contributing constructively to a multidisciplinary team.

It would be a plus if you have:

• 
Experience with robotics, UAVs, autonomous systems, or flight control software.

• 
Familiarity with ArduPilot, PX4, MAVLink, or similar technologies.

• 
Experience with simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or real-time systems.

• 
Knowledge of networking, telemetry, data acquisition, or distributed systems.

• 
Experience using AI-assisted development tools or working with machine learning technologies.

We don't expect you to tick every box. We're more interested in your engineering mindset, technical curiosity, and ability to learn.

As an early-stage startup pushing the boundaries of innovation, we offer a salary typical for our phase of growth.

About Acodyne

Acodyne is on a mission to develop the world's fastest unmanned eVTOL aircraft for heavy payloads, initially to serve off-shore, remote areas and general logistics.

Beyond developing the aircraft, we're exploring how intelligent software, automation, and data-driven systems can shape the future of unmanned cargo operations.

We are a small, ambitious engineering team with plans to grow significantly. We're based at Avedøre Airfield, where your daily work will primarily take place.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and interviews will be conducted continuously.

Please note that we are currently unable to provide visa sponsorship or relocation assistance.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

We are looking for a Product Compliance Manager to join Veo's newly established Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team.

As Veo continues to grow, we navigate a broad range of regulatory requirements across our products and business, from certifications, product safety, and environmental regulation to market access and broader compliance obligations.

In this role, you will focus on product-related regulatory compliance and certifications, while also working across Veo's broader compliance agenda. You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

You will join a small GRC team with a broad mandate and significant exposure across Veo. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys understanding regulation, technology, and business.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

• Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

• Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

• Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

• Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

• Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

• Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

• Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

• Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

• Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

• Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

Contact Martin Eger Larsen one mel@veo.co if you have any questions

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

**About Apylon And The Opportunity

**Apylon is building agents for the most complex workflow out there - financial admin in healthcare.

Hospitals and payers move billions of euros through fragmented, manual workflows shaped by clinical data, payer rules, contracts, and local coding systems. We believe this is a data, machine-learning, and automation problem disguised as financial operations.

We are live with leading private hospitals and expanding quickly. Every hospital presents a different challenge: EHR systems are configured differently, national coding rules vary, and contracts describe the same clinical event in different terms. Your job is to help us turn that complexity into a system that learns: each new integration should make the next one faster, safer, and less expensive.

Apylon is backed by experienced operators and top-tier investors in healthcare and fintech. Our team draws on experience from Zendesk, Pleo, Wawa Fertility, Sibill, and some of the largest multi-country hospital groups in Europe. You’ll join the first small engineering team, with massive ownership over both what we build and how we build it.

Delivering healthcare is hard. Getting paid for it shouldn’t be.

You’ll be responsible for

• Own EHR integrations end to end: APIs, schemas, undocumented behaviour, operational failure modes, and vendor changes.

• Build reusable integration-platform primitives for extraction, normalisation, versioning, replay, monitoring, and observability.

• Design the canonical data model that connects heterogeneous EHR data, reimbursement systems, national coding standards, and hospital-specific conventions.

• Build reliable inputs for our billing agents, including the constraints, validation, and evaluation systems that make model-assisted decisions safe to use in production.

• Work directly with hospital IT teams and EHR vendors: technical discovery, implementation, joint debugging, and onboarding.

• Take responsibility for the full lifecycle of your work: design, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and iteration from real-world data.

Who you are

• 3+ years building and operating production systems in complex, messy domains. We care more about demonstrated judgment and ownership than an exact number of years.

• Experience using LLMs as production components—not just developer tools. You understand when to use models, when deterministic systems are better, how to constrain outputs, and how to evaluate reliability.

• Strong data-modelling instincts. You know when abstraction creates leverage and when it hides important real-world variation.

• Comfort working from incomplete information. You form hypotheses, test them against data, and distinguish unknowns that can wait from assumptions that could invalidate the system.

• Confidence in customer-facing technical work: discovery calls, debugging sessions, and direct conversations with vendors and hospital IT teams.

• Experience with cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.

• A practical, hands-on approach: equally comfortable designing an integration architecture and writing a quick script to answer an urgent question.

This role may be a strong fit if

You enjoy reverse-engineering systems you do not control, finding structure in messy real-world data, and turning one-off discoveries into reusable software. You are comfortable being the engineer in the room with customers and partners.

What this role is not

• Consulting or bespoke delivery work. Each integration must improve the product and reduce the marginal cost of the next.

• A role insulated from customers or operational reality.

• Pure platform engineering or pure integration work: the value comes from doing both.

• A role where incorrect mappings are merely technical defects. In this domain, they can produce incorrect invoices.

Bonus points

• Experience with healthcare interoperability or coding standards, including HL7v2, FHIR, or national messaging and reimbursement standards.

• Experience building and operating third-party integrations at scale.

• Experience in healthcare, fintech, or another regulated environment.

• Experience in an early-stage or fast-growing company.

• Working proficiency in Danish, or German.

Our tech stack

• Python

• Django

• React

• PostgreSQL

• AWS

• K8s

• Terraform

• Bedrock

• We’re pragmatic. You’ll have a big say in how it evolves.

What Apylon offers

• The chance to solve one of Europe’s biggest healthcare inefficiencies.

• Competitive salary + stock options (you’ll own part of what you build).

• 25 days of annual leave + local public holidays.

• Lunch on us during workdays at the office.

• Regular off-sites and social events. We like building together, not just working together.

• Travel within the EU roughly monthly. Onboarding a hospital, working through an integration with a vendor’s engineers, or spending time on-site to understand how the data is actually produced. If travelling to a hospital basement to figure out why an export is malformed sounds like a bad week, this isn’t your role.

Working at Apylon means embarking on a highly ambitious mission to rebuild the financial infrastructure of European healthcare. We’re already live with leading private hospitals, processing thousands of invoices, proving that complex payer rules can be turned into code, powering transparent, automated, and intelligent revenue systems.

How to apply. If you're excited by the challenge of building intelligent, high-impact systems at the core of European healthcare and enjoy shipping fast, we'd love to hear from you.
